title: Predictive Queue Slimming and Soft-Deny Proxy for Dedicated Pools
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a compact, tenant-aware admission proxy that reduces tail latency and preserves throughput guarantees during overload by combining short-horizon predictive autoscaling signals, queue slimming (aging-based drop+reweight), and a soft-deny escalation path that degrades non-critical requests before impacting reserved throughput.

Motivation: Existing fleet-level shedder solutions are either too coarse (global drop) or too aggressive (hard-deny), causing flaky customer experience for latency-sensitive tenants. This ticket designs a per-edge admission proxy that enforces tenant contracts deterministically while enabling smoother degradation and faster recovery.

Scope:
- Admission proxy sidecar deployed in front of dedicated pool ingress (per-region).
- Predictive signal consumer: short-window autoscaler forecasts + recent queue growth + token-bucket headroom.
- Queue slimming strategy: time-decay ranks requests by priority and approximate cost, trim low-ranked requests when queue > threshold.
- Soft-deny escalation: return structured 202-with-retry-metadata or instruct SDKs to slow-progress (client-visible backoff hint) before returning hard 429s.
- Token reservations: maintain minimal deterministic reservation for high-SLO tenants (configurable per-contract).
- Observability: per-tenant queue histogram, soft-deny rate, drop-reason tags, recovery time metrics, and synthetic eval hooks.

Success criteria:
- Reduce p95 generation latency spikes during overload by >=30% for latency-SLO tenants.
- Maintain committed throughput for reserved tenants (<=5% violation window outside planned maintenance).
- Decrease hard 429s by 50% in simulated 2x sudden surge scenarios by using soft-deny path.

Non-goals:
- Replacing centralized fleet admission policy (this complements existing router-level shims).
- Deep model-aware cost estimation (approximate cost heuristics suffice for v1).
test_plan: Unit tests for queue ranking and slimming logic (deterministic seed)
Integration test with local dedicated pool simulator and spike generator
Chaos test: node failure and rapid restart while soft-deny enabled
Golden traffic replay comparing current shedder vs soft-deny proxy
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime 'pqss-proxy'—start with 1% of tenants in us-west1
Progressive ramp: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks with automated rollback on SLO regressions
Enable token reservation only for tenants with explicit contract and opt-in
migration_notes: Provide migration tool to backfill per-tenant priority config from billing/contract DB
Add SDK change to respect soft-deny 202-with-retry-metadata (backwards compatible)
risks: SDK adoption lag: clients may not honor soft-deny hints leading to higher retries
Prediction errors could oscillate admission limits if autoscaler forecasts are noisy
Edge-side state increases operational complexity for upgrades
mitigations: Constrain predictor smoothing and add dampening window (exponential backoff on aggressive changes)
Fallback to conservative static thresholds if predictor variance exceeds bound
Canary rollout and kill-switch config to revert to global shedder quickly
